quotes.text: With deterministic tools, the human decides, and the tool executes. With cognitive systems, the tool proposes, and the human must decide.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures the core inversion of responsibility that generative AI forces on organizations.

quotes.text: AI doesn't scale competence first. It scales whatever is already true in your environment. If your data is messy, it scales mess.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A crisp explanation of why AI amplifies existing weaknesses instead of fixing them.

quotes.text: Prompt volume is usually a proxy for unclear intent or missing authority. People keep rewriting prompts because they can't state what they actually need or they refuse to commit to the trade-offs they're asking for.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Challenges the belief that better prompting is the path to better AI results.

quotes.text: Thinking without enforcement is fantasy. Enforcement without thinking is bureaucracy. Your job is to build the middle, where AI can propose, humans can judge, and the system can enforce consequences with no deniability.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Condenses the episode's governance model into a memorable formula.

quotes.text: Can a human defend the decision without mentioning the AI? If the answer is no, you didn't make a decision. You delegated one and you delegated it to a system that cannot be accountable.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Offers a simple, practical test for whether judgment was outsourced to AI.

chapters.title: Why tool metaphors fail for Copilot
AI scales ambiguity faster than capability
Scenarios: security, HR and IT change

takeaways: Copilot is a probabilistic cognition engine, so its output must be treated as a proposal that a named human accepts or rejects, not as an answer.
More prompts, prompt libraries and delayed training cannot replace clear intent, explicit constraints, decision rights and governance that is actually enforced.
Decision logs, judgment moments embedded in workflows and named individual decision owners connect AI cognition to accountable action.
hook: Many organizations roll out Copilot, measure adoption and quietly let plausible AI output stand in for human decisions. This episode is for leaders, architects and Microsoft 365 teams who want AI to scale capability instead of confusion, and shows how to put judgment, ownership and enforcement back into the workflow.
